native.admission_inspect: A thin horn square. Four edges meet, yet the grain at one corner arrives a breath late.
apply_texts: A careful press. The corner yields, the grain lags, and the square stays shut on every side.
Aligned to your eye, the four sides close. The grain does not, and the room is not the cause.
Pressed flat, it rocks once. The late corner is smaller than before, and no less sure.
The horn is nearly still. One short edge remains, too small now to argue with.
The horn takes the press unevenly. Three edges hold; the fourth reports the touch too late.
The last give in the horn is small. One edge thins, then the figure pretends to be finished.
The mismatch is familiar. You leave the square as it lies, no larger than a tired angle.
The short corner returns sooner. Warmth remains; agreement does not.
The square rocks on a point no edge should own. The grain is still one breath behind.
Warm horn under the thumb. For a moment every edge agrees, and then one is short again.
You press the late corner. It gives a hair, and the other edges answer a moment out of order.
You set it flat again. It is a square. The lagging corner makes that word feel slightly false.
You stop trying to face the missing turn. The square remains square, and that is the limit.
inspect_texts: A thin horn square. Four edges meet, yet the grain at one corner arrives a breath late.
Again the grain lags. From here the figure is only a square, which does not settle the eye.
Inside your frame it is a square. The late grain implies a facing you cannot turn to meet.
Square to the thumb, flat to the eye. One edge answers as if a turn were left unfinished.
The corner you noted is still late. Light on the far edge is one shade thinner than the rest.
The horn is only warm and square. A short corner comes and goes with the angle of the light.
The lag has a rhythm. The corner arrives later each time, and the square grows no squarer.
The lamina does not open. It only shows that your edges and its edges are not the same count.
The same four sides. Your measure closes; the horn grain does not, by a breath of angle.
You know this flatness. The unmatched edge is smaller than your doubt, and still not flush.
native.name: Late Horn Square
